title: HTTPS and what encryption costs you

claims.text: The version of the protocol specified in RFC 8446 in August 2018 reduces the full handshake to a single round trip, the client speculatively sending its key share in the first message so that encryption can begin after one exchange rather than two. It also mandates forward secrecy through ephemeral key exchange and removes the legacy cipher suites.

source.title: RFC 8446, The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3, E. Rescorla, August 2018

claims.text: The zero round trip mode saves a further exchange at the cost of stated security properties: that data is not forward secret, since it is encrypted solely under keys derived from the offered pre-shared key, and there are no guarantees of non-replay between connections, because protection for ordinary data comes from the server's random value and this data does not depend on it.

source.title: RFC 8446, The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3, E. Rescorla, August 2018

claims.text: The specification requires that any server instance — machine, thread or other entity in the serving infrastructure — accept such early data for the same handshake at most once, which limits replays to the number of server instances in the deployment rather than eliminating them.

source.title: RFC 8446, The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3, E. Rescorla, August 2018

beats.broke: the network carries your bytes past machines you do not control, any of which can read them, alter them, or pretend to be the other end
beats.fix: negotiate keys at the start of the connection and encrypt everything after, with certificates binding an identity to a key so the other end can be checked rather than assumed
beats.cost: the negotiation is round trips before any useful byte moves, and the optimisation that removes the last round trip gives up forward secrecy and replay protection for the data it carries
beats.interview: what the fastest mode of this protocol gives up, and which requests may safely use it
